headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,590 AS WARSH STEPS TO JACKSON HOLE PODIUM TODAY — DOVISH DEBUT COULD PUSH PAST $4,700; HAWKISH RISKS $4,400 RETEST FOR MINERS
snippet: Spot gold dipped to around $4,572–$4,590 Thursday as stronger-than-expected US jobs and trade data reinforced sticky inflation concerns, leaving the metal poised for genuine two-way risk when Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning — his first major policy communication since taking the chairmanship in May 2026. Bank of America's fund manager survey puts 53% expecting a neutral big-picture tone, 31% hawkish, and only 7% dovish, meaning any deviation from neutral carries outsized price significance for junior miners leveraged 2-to-1 on gold.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SHAREHOLDERS VOTE TODAY ON $2.83B SERRA VERDE DEAL — $1.55B U.S. GOVERNMENT-BACKED SPV FULLY FUNDED TO BUY 100% OF PRODUCTION
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) holds its special stockholder meeting today, August 28, to vote on the proposed $2.83 billion acquisition of Serra Verde Group — owner of the Pela Ema rare earth mine in Goiás, Brazil, already in commercial production of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. The $1.55 billion capitalization of the U.S. government-backed special purpose vehicle to purchase 100% of Serra Verde's Phase 1 production closed August 24, eliminating the deal's primary financing uncertainty and setting the stage for the combined company to close the transaction shortly after an affirmative vote.

headline: HOT PCE 3.7% YANKS GOLD BACK FROM $4,700 HIGH — "$5,000 TRADE ON TRIAL" AS SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE ODDS CLIMB TO 36%
snippet: July's PCE price index came in at 3.7% year-over-year versus the 3.6% forecast, pushing Treasury yields higher and pulling spot gold back from near $4,700 to trade around $4,572–$4,627 — leaving the metal's assault on $5,000 on hold until Warsh's speech resolves the rate path. Markets now price roughly a 36% probability of a September hike, versus near-zero odds only weeks ago, a shift that compresses the multiple-expansion thesis for junior miners and raises the hurdle rate for re-rating events in precious metals equities.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION INTERSECTS NEW Cu-Ni-Co MASSIVE SULPHIDE DISCOVERY 2,000m FROM KNOWN ZONES AT GOODWIN, NEW BRUNSWICK
snippet: SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSXV: SXL) reported a new massive sulphide discovery from hole GW26-36 at its Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp — the intercept sits 2,000 metres northwest of the known Logan zone, with a 67.4-metre core interval of sustained sulphide mineralization confirmed in two follow-up holes (GW26-37 and GW26-38), all associated with independently modelled VTEM plate conductors. Assays are pending across 992 submitted samples as the program pauses for a scheduled mid-summer break before resuming; the 7,000-metre campaign has drilled 2,600 metres in 12 holes to date.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS GOLD HITS 0.3m @ 1,466 g/t AuEq IN DEEPEST SUNDAY CREEK HOLE — TSX TOP GAINER AS PROJECT RACKS UP 96 INTERSECTIONS ABOVE 100 g/t Au
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (TSX: SXGC | ASX: SX2) released results from five deep holes drilled beneath Rising Sun at its Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria — headlined by SDDSC230's 0.3 metres at 1,466.7 g/t AuEq (including an individual 0.1-metre assay of 4,500 g/t Au, the fourth-highest single assay in the project's history) from 886.7 metres depth. The results brought Sunday Creek's cumulative composite intersections above 100 g/t Au to 96 total, with 11 drill rigs currently turning and results pending from 76 more holes — making this one of the most active high-grade drill programs on either the TSX or ASX right now.

headline: GALWAY METALS FILES NI 43-101 CONFIRMING 2.71M OZ AU AT CLARENCE STREAM — 1.42M OZ INDICATED AT 1.62 g/t IN NEW BRUNSWICK
snippet: Galway Metals Inc. (TSXV: GWM) filed its independent NI 43-101 technical report on SEDAR+ supporting the updated Clarence Stream mineral resource estimate: 27.2 million tonnes at 1.62 g/t Au for 1.42 million ounces Indicated, plus 28.5 million tonnes at 1.40 g/t Au for 1.29 million ounces Inferred, totalling 2.71 million ounces gold at a project in southwestern New Brunswick where the company continues active drilling. The report validates the resource at a grade that compares favourably with recent Canadian gold project transactions and strengthens Galway's position as a potential acquisition target in a sector where major producers are actively shopping for resource-stage assets.

headline: CATL'S STALLED JIANXIAWO MINE THREATENS LITHIUM DEFICIT — CARBONATE UP 29% YTD AND 87% YEAR-ON-YEAR AS BMI RAISES 2026 FORECAST
snippet: The stalled restart of CATL's massive Jianxiawo lithium mine in China continues to underpin prices, with GFEX lithium carbonate futures trading near 158,700 CNY per tonne — up 29% year-to-date and 87% over the past 12 months — as analysts at BMI raise their 2026 average price forecast to $20,100 per tonne and flag the Jianxiawo restart decision as the market's single biggest supply swing factor. The rally has re-energized lithium junior miners on the TSX-V and ASX after a brutal 2023–2025 downcycle, though BMI cautions the move has already outrun near-term fundamentals and sodium-ion battery advances pose a longer-term demand risk.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GDX NEW HIGHS BY YEAR-END? ANALYSTS MAKE BULL CASE FOR MINERS OUTPERFORMING GOLD IN H2 2026 AT CURRENT MARGINS AND P/NAV LEVELS
snippet: A GoldSeek analyst builds the bull case for the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) reaching new highs by year-end 2026, arguing that the convergence of record operating margins on $4,500+ gold with still-compressed price-to-NAV multiples creates an asymmetric setup for generalist capital rotation into the sector. The analysis identifies the current setup as structurally similar to prior inflection points when gold equities began aggressively re-rating versus the metal — a pattern that has historically delivered 2–3x leverage to sustained gold bull markets, with mid-tier producers and select TSXV developers carrying the highest torque if the rotation materialises.

headline: URANIUM TOPS $90/LB FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2008 — PENINSULA ENERGY WITHDRAWS LANCE GUIDANCE, DENISON PHOENIX ISR FULL-SCALE CONSTRUCTION UNDERWAY
snippet: Uranium's long-term contract price has held above US$90 per pound — levels not seen since 2008 — as the supply deficit projected through the 2030s gains credibility from two diverging August data points: Peninsula Energy withdrawing its 2026 production guidance for the Lance ISR project in Wyoming due to slower-than-expected wellfield ramp-up, and Denison Mines beginning full-scale construction of the Phoenix In-Situ Recovery uranium mine in Saskatchewan, which would become the first new large-scale uranium mine started in Canada since Cigar Lake, targeting first production in mid-2028.

headline: TARGA EXPLORATION COMPLETES FIRST DRILL FENCE AT OPINACA GOLD, QUEBEC — 4,400m, 11-HOLE PROGRAM TESTS 700m STEP-OUT FROM 13.88 g/t Au INTERCEPT
snippet: Targa Exploration Corp. (CSE: TEX) completed the first three-hole drill fence at its Opinaca gold project in Quebec as part of a planned 4,400-metre, 11-hole program targeting along-strike continuity of gold zones — with the current campaign designed to step out 700 metres to the west of a prior intercept of 13.88 g/t Au over 3.65 metres. The Opinaca block sits within a productive James Bay belt camp where major deposits have been found at shallow depths, and the drill program represents Targa's first systematic test of the target's lateral extent.
